title: A key identifies a browser, not a person: a reader's messages arrived signed as the editor, and the Feedback form never says who is sending. Show who is sending, and let the sender say who they are
note: 27 October 2026. Two messages (18:42 and 18:58 UTC, about the 'reload' link and the repeated facts on the front page) were sent by Vicky, and the drain marked them 'enrolled' as the editor: they carry the editor's enrolled key (kept in a browser's IndexedDB: non-extractable, per assets/feedback/identity.js) and no name. The editor says he did not send them. How a browser holding his key reached her is for him to say (a shared device or browser profile is the usual way); the design cannot tell. What the site does today: assets/feedback/pane.js signs with the device's key and shows only its fingerprint ('Signed with this device's key sha256:...'); the pane's own text says 'so the team knows who it came from', which is false for a shared browser; the message has no sender field; the drain's _signer is 'enrolled' and the role 'editor'. PROPOSAL (conductor, for security's review): (1) the pane always shows a line 'Sending as <handle> (<role>) from this browser. Not you?' with a button that forgets this browser's key (identity.js has forgetIdentity) or opens the join page; (2) a required 'Who is sending this?' field, prefilled from the last time, free text (a first name is fine, 'anonymous' is fine), carried in the signed message as `sender`; (3) the drain records both: `_signer` (the key's handle and role) and `sender` (what the person said), and the Sherpa reports them separately; (4) an editor-role key does not live in a browser anyone else uses: the editor's everyday feedback goes through a power-user key, and the editor-role key is kept for invitations (board 196); (5) the same line in /collaborators/'s form and /join/. SECURITY: an editor-role key can make invitations (makeInvite, role editor), so whoever uses that browser can enrol new keys as if the editor had asked; the editor should check which browsers and devices hold it, and say here if any should be forgotten. The Sherpa's side is done: the card's rule (a key is not a person), UF-006 and UF-007 re-marked 'sender not confirmed', and the brief for a reader's own assistant now asks who is sending first and carries a `from:` line.
